messages:
mira: Heads-up — since ~06:20 UTC eu-west-1 p4 pools are showing short, repeatable GPU capacity drops (20% dips for 10–30s). Not a full OOM, more like a 'sag' where scheduler marks some GPUs unavailable then they come back. infra-bot posted an alert.

sam: Can you paste the alert/findings?

mira: infra-bot: ALERT gpu-health eu-west-1/p4 pool: intermittent device state transitions detected (NVML code 4). Recent node list:
```
node-az1-rack12 p4-16 10:21:34 UNHEALTHY
node-az1-rack14 p4-16 10:22:12 UNHEALTHY
node-az2-rack03 p4-16 10:24:01 UNHEALTHY
```
Pattern looks rack-local, not full AZ.

alex: Interesting — NVML code 4 = device lost/reset? Could be PDU or thermal/trip causing PCIe reset. Any rack power-cycle logs from the BMC?

mira: I'm pulling BMC logs now. Quick grep shows repeated npm: "pdu_event: breaker_trip" on rack12 and rack14 around the same minutes. Not seeing whole-host reboots, just PDUs toggling load shed.

tj: Rack-level PDU cycling would explain transient device resets without node OS reboot. That matches GPU FLR behavior. If true, those GPUs get gated and scheduler marks them unavailable until NVML recovers.

sam: How widespread? Are tenants impacted or just background jobs?

mira: Early, looks like best-effort jobs saw higher latency and a few preemptible slots dropped. No customer-facing SLA alerts yet, but two Dedicated slices saw short 5–10s tail latencies.

alex: Two quick mitigations: 1) soft-shield affected racks (stop new allocations) 2) add reactive routing rule to avoid eu-west-1 p4 pool for high-SLO tenants until we confirm stability.

mira: Agreed. I'm opening a soft-drain for rack12 and rack14 (kubectl cordon + annotate) and adding a routing override for routed-tenants (canary first). Command I ran:
```
kubectl annotate node node-az1-rack12 avoid-scheduling=transient-pdu
kubectl cordon node-az1-rack12
```

tj: Also start pre-warming spare capacity in eu-west-2 and eu-central, then shift critical slices via routing policy for 30m window. We'll need to accept some egress cost for cross-region traffic. Quick calc: shifting 10k tokens/s for 30m ~ estimate $120 in egress.

sam: Fine for short window. Can we automate fallback routing for tenants with higher latency sensitivity? Maybe update routing policy to prefer same-AZ then same-region then fallback to eu-west-2.

alex: Yep — I'll push a canary policy that tags high-SLO tenants and routes them off eu-west-1 p4 if device_flap_rate > 0.1 over 5m.

mira: BMC team says they see PDUs reporting upstream breaker trips probably due to scheduled maintenance in the colo (but not announced). I'm reaching out to colo ops to confirm. If this is maintenance, we should schedule a planned capacity migration next time rather than reactive.

infra-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: created ticket INF-3429 linking pdu events + nvml resets; severity: medium; owner: alex.

tj: Action list: 1) keep soft-drain on affected racks for now 2) apply canary routing for high-SLO tenants (alex) 3) pre-warm eu-west-2 pools (tj) 4) confirm with colo ops and get ETA (mira) 5) cost owner will approve cross-region egress (sam).

mira: I'll also schedule a post-mortem on whether we should proactively shield racks showing >2 PDU events in 10m and whether our autoscaling should preemptively spin up cold nodes in other regions.

sam: Minor note — we should update runbooks: add a quick check for PDU/trip in addition to NVML when seeing transient device gating.

alex: Will do. Pushing policy now, canary for 5 tenants first.

mira: Thanks — keeping an eye. If colo confirms planned work, we'll convert to planned maintenance and coordinate migration. :eyes:
